papers.title: VisPan: Real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Infectious diseases persist as a major global public health challenge. Diverse factors, including climate change, globalization, deforestation, human-animal interactions, lifestyle choices, and various biological factors, can contribute to their emergence and reemergence. Rapid detection and characterization of (re)emerging pathogens are therefore critical for effective outbreak management and for enhancing our understanding of epidemics by monitoring the transmission, spread, evolution, and genomics of pathogens. In this context, next-generation sequencing technologies (NGS), particularly long-read platforms such as Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT), have opened new avenues for real-time pathogen monitoring. However, the bioinformatics bottleneck remains a challenge, emphasizing the need for efficient, accessible, and user-friendly analysis tools. Results Here, we present a tool adapted from the RAMPART software that enables real-time data visualisation of multiplex PCR syndromic panels combined with Oxford Nanopore sequencing. This real-time analysis enables rapid pathogen detection, from raw data acquisition to taxonomic assignment, within minutes. The interface offers dynamic visual tracking of the sequencing run and amplicon coverage, facilitating immediate insights during diagnostic workflows. Validation experiments confirmed the system’s reliability, accurately identifying all pathogens present in complex clinical or environmental samples. This tool provides an integrated, user-friendly solution for genomic pathogen surveillance in field or clinical settings

papers.title: HisCMCL: Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning with Hierarchical Multi-Scale Fusion for Spatial Expression Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation High costs and operational complexity limit the clinical application of spatial transcriptomics (ST). Inferring ST from pathology images is a promising alternative, the core of which lies in effectively aligning image and gene expression features. However, existing models are mostly limited to single-scale and single-slice modeling. This not only fails to connect microscopic cells with macroscopic tissues but also restricts generalization due to the inability to extract cross-sample shared features. Furthermore, the inherent representational differences between modalities further exacerbate the difficulty of feature alignment. Results To address these challenges, we propose HisCMCL, a multimodal framework. The model combines multi-scale features with a cross-attention mechanism to jointly capture local morphology and global context. Additionally, it fuses spatial location information and utilizes a contrastive learning strategy to facilitate the effective alignment of image and transcriptomic features. Evaluations on four public datasets demonstrate that HisCMCL outperforms existing baseline methods in predictive performance. It exhibits good structural consistency in identifying cancer and immune markers and delineating tumor regions, offering new insights for spatial expression inference. Availability and implementation The code of HisCMCL is available at https://github.com/wenwenmin/HisCMCL

Inferring ST from pathology images is a promising alternative, the core of which lies in effectively aligning image and gene expression features. This not only fails to connect microscopic cells with macroscopic tissues but also restricts generalization due to the inability to extract cross-sample shared features. Furthermore, the inherent representational differences between modalities further exacerbate the difficulty of feature alignment.

RESULTS: To address these challenges, we propose HisCMCL, a multimodal framework. The model combines multi-scale features with a cross-attention mechanism to jointly capture local morphology and global context. Additionally, it fuses spatial location information and utilizes a contrastive learning strategy to facilitate the effective alignment of image and transcriptomic features. Evaluations on four public datasets demonstrate that HisCMCL outperforms existing baseline methods in predictive performance. It exhibits good structural consistency in identifying cancer and immune markers and delineating tumor regions, offering new insights for spatial expression inference.

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
高昂的成本与复杂的操作流程限制了空间转录组学的临床应用。从病理图像中推断空间转录组信息是一种具有前景的替代方法，其关键在于有效匹配图像特征与基因表达数据。然而现有模型大多仅局限于单尺度、单层样本的分析，这种局限性不仅无法将微观细胞结构与宏观组织形态联系起来，还因无法提取跨样本共性特征而限制了模型的泛化能力。此外，不同模态数据在表征方式上的本质差异进一步加剧了特征匹配的难度。  

为应对这些挑战，我们提出了HisCMCL这一多模态框架。该模型结合了多尺度特征与交叉注意力机制，既能捕捉局部结构信息，又能反映整体组织环境；同时通过融合空间位置数据并采用对比学习策略，有效实现了图像特征与转录组数据的匹配。在四个公开数据集上的测试结果表明，HisCMCL在预测性能上显著优于现有方法，在识别癌症相关标志物、区分肿瘤区域等方面也表现出良好的稳定性，为空间表达信息的分析提供了新的思路。  

**代码获取方式**  
HisCMCL的源代码可访问以下链接下载：  
https://github.com/wenwenmin/HisCMCL

为应对这些挑战，我们提出了HisCMCL这一多模态分析框架。该模型结合了多尺度特征与交叉注意力机制，既能捕捉局部组织结构信息，又能反映整体环境特征；同时通过融合空间位置数据并采用对比学习策略，有效实现了图像数据与转录组数据的匹配。在四个公开数据集上的测试结果表明，HisCMCL在预测性能上显著优于现有方法，其在识别癌症相关标志物、区分肿瘤区域等方面的表现也体现了良好的稳定性，为空间表达信息的分析提供了新的思路。
papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: High costs and operational complexity limit the clinical application of spatial transcriptomics (ST). Inferring ST from pathology images is a promising alternative, the core of which lies in effectively aligning image and gene expression features. However, existing models are mostly limited to single-scale and single-slice modeling. This not only fails to connect microscopic cells with macroscopic tissues but also restricts generalization due to the inability to extract cross-sample shared features. Furthermore, the inherent representational differences between modalities further exacerbate the difficulty of feature alignment.

RESULTS: To address these challenges, we propose HisCMCL, a multimodal framework. The model combines multi-scale features with a cross-attention mechanism to jointly capture local morphology and global context. Additionally, it fuses spatial location information and utilizes a contrastive learning strategy to facilitate the effective alignment of image and transcriptomic features. Evaluations on four public datasets demonstrate that HisCMCL outperforms existing baseline methods in predictive performance. It exhibits good structural consistency in identifying cancer and immune markers and delineating tumor regions, offering new insights for spatial expression inference.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The code of HisCMCL is available at https://github.com/wenwenmin/HisCMCL.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.title: Genomics-Informed Approach Identifies Which Cell Types Regulate the Metabolome
papers.summary: Abstract Metabolism occurs in a cell type-specific manner, but which cells regulate metabolite levels remains unclear. Here, we integrate some of the largest metabolite quantitative trait loci datasets, TOPMed and UK Biobank, with one of the most extensive single-cell RNA sequencing resources, Tabula Sapiens. This integration allows us to identify cell types that regulate metabolites body-wide. We find hepatocytes are the primary regulatory cell type for most metabolites, associating with 385/410 (94%) metabolites for whom an association is found. Additionally, our multi-gene approach reveals more metabolite associations with beta cells compared to those identified using a single-gene approach. For example, we identify novel metabolite-cell type associations, such as the association between phenylpropanoic acid and beta cells, this metabolite that was previously thought to be regulated by the microbiome

all_papers.title: VisPan: Real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Infectious diseases persist as a major global public health challenge. Diverse factors, including climate change, globalization, deforestation, human-animal interactions, lifestyle choices, and various biological factors, can contribute to their emergence and reemergence. Rapid detection and characterization of (re)emerging pathogens are therefore critical for effective outbreak management and for enhancing our understanding of epidemics by monitoring the transmission, spread, evolution, and genomics of pathogens. In this context, next-generation sequencing technologies (NGS), particularly long-read platforms such as Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT), have opened new avenues for real-time pathogen monitoring. However, the bioinformatics bottleneck remains a challenge, emphasizing the need for efficient, accessible, and user-friendly analysis tools. Results Here, we present a tool adapted from the RAMPART software that enables real-time data visualisation of multiplex PCR syndromic panels combined with Oxford Nanopore sequencing. This real-time analysis enables rapid pathogen detection, from raw data acquisition to taxonomic assignment, within minutes. The interface offers dynamic visual tracking of the sequencing run and amplicon coverage, facilitating immediate insights during diagnostic workflows. Validation experiments confirmed the system’s reliability, accurately identifying all pathogens present in complex clinical or environmental samples. This tool provides an integrated, user-friendly solution for genomic pathogen surveillance in field or clinical settings

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
传染病始终是全球公共卫生的主要挑战。气候变化、全球化、森林砍伐、人与动物的相互作用、生活方式的选择以及各种生物因素等都可能促成这些疾病的出现与再次传播。因此，快速检测并分析这些新出现的或重新出现的病原体对于有效控制疫情至关重要，同时也有助于我们通过监测病原体的传播机制、进化过程及其基因组特征来加深对流行病的理解。在这一背景下，下一代测序技术，尤其是像牛津纳米孔技术公司提供的长读长测序平台，为实时监测病原体提供了新的途径。然而，生物信息学分析方面的瓶颈依然存在，这凸显出开发高效、易用且用户友好的分析工具的必要性。  

**结果**

MOTIVATION: Infectious diseases persist as a major global public health challenge. Diverse factors, including climate change, globalization, deforestation, human-animal interactions, lifestyle choices, and various biological factors, can contribute to their emergence and reemergence. Rapid detection and characterization of (re)emerging pathogens are therefore critical for effective outbreak management and for enhancing our understanding of epidemics by monitoring the transmission, spread, evolution, and genomics of pathogens. In this context, next-generation sequencing technologies (NGS), particularly long-read platforms such as Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT), have opened new avenues for real-time pathogen monitoring. However, the bioinformatics bottleneck remains a challenge, emphasizing the need for efficient, accessible, and user-friendly analysis tools.

RESULTS: Here, we present a tool adapted from the RAMPART software that enables real-time data visualisation of multiplex PCR syndromic panels combined with Oxford Nanopore sequencing. This real-time analysis enables rapid pathogen detection, from raw data acquisition to taxonomic assignment, within minutes. The interface offers dynamic visual tracking of the sequencing run and amplicon coverage, facilitating immediate insights during diagnostic workflows. Validation experiments confirmed the system's reliability, accurately identifying all pathogens present in complex clinical or environmental samples. This tool provides an integrated, user-friendly solution for genomic pathogen surveillance in field or clinical settings.

all_papers.title: HisCMCL: Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning with Hierarchical Multi-Scale Fusion for Spatial Expression Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation High costs and operational complexity limit the clinical application of spatial transcriptomics (ST). Inferring ST from pathology images is a promising alternative, the core of which lies in effectively aligning image and gene expression features. However, existing models are mostly limited to single-scale and single-slice modeling. This not only fails to connect microscopic cells with macroscopic tissues but also restricts generalization due to the inability to extract cross-sample shared features. Furthermore, the inherent representational differences between modalities further exacerbate the difficulty of feature alignment. Results To address these challenges, we propose HisCMCL, a multimodal framework. The model combines multi-scale features with a cross-attention mechanism to jointly capture local morphology and global context. Additionally, it fuses spatial location information and utilizes a contrastive learning strategy to facilitate the effective alignment of image and transcriptomic features. Evaluations on four public datasets demonstrate that HisCMCL outperforms existing baseline methods in predictive performance. It exhibits good structural consistency in identifying cancer and immune markers and delineating tumor regions, offering new insights for spatial expression inference. Availability and implementation The code of HisCMCL is available at https://github.com/wenwenmin/HisCMCL

all_papers.title: Genomics-Informed Approach Identifies Which Cell Types Regulate the Metabolome
all_papers.summary: Abstract Metabolism occurs in a cell type-specific manner, but which cells regulate metabolite levels remains unclear. Here, we integrate some of the largest metabolite quantitative trait loci datasets, TOPMed and UK Biobank, with one of the most extensive single-cell RNA sequencing resources, Tabula Sapiens. This integration allows us to identify cell types that regulate metabolites body-wide. We find hepatocytes are the primary regulatory cell type for most metabolites, associating with 385/410 (94%) metabolites for whom an association is found. Additionally, our multi-gene approach reveals more metabolite associations with beta cells compared to those identified using a single-gene approach. For example, we identify novel metabolite-cell type associations, such as the association between phenylpropanoic acid and beta cells, this metabolite that was previously thought to be regulated by the microbiome

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Metabolism occurs in a cell type-specific manner, but which cells regulate metabolite levels remains unclear. Here, we integrate some of the largest metabolite quantitative trait loci datasets, TOPMed and UK Biobank, with one of the most extensive single-cell RNA sequencing resources, Tabula Sapiens. This integration allows us to identify cell types that regulate metabolites body-wide. We find hepatocytes are the primary regulatory cell type for most metabolites, associating with 385/410 (94%) metabolites for whom an association is found. Additionally, our multi-gene approach reveals more metabolite associations with beta cells compared to those identified using a single-gene approach.
